newsitem.title: UK: Peugeot faces UK industrial action deadline.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot faces UK industrial action deadline.

text.p: British workers at French car-maker PSA Peugeot Citroen's Coventry plant have agreed an overtime ban starting from March 14 and plan an all-out strike the week after unless the company agrees to negotiate on pay and conditions, unions said on Thursday.

The Transport and General (T&G) union and the Amalgamated Engineering and Electricians (AEEU) union said company bosses have until March 21 to open talks or face an indefinite strike which could involve up to 3,000 of Peugeot's British workers.
A spokesman for Peugeot said it had not yet been informed of the decision. "Until we get an official report we cannot comment on the impact it will have," he said.
But a spokesman for the T&G trade union said that the intervening period would give Peugeot chiefs the time to enter talks.
"This is a wake-up call for Peugeot management, " T&G national officer for the motor industry Tony Woodley said in a statement.

"There is still time for them to avert industrial action by agreeing at long last to sit down with the unions and seriously address our wages and conditions claim and their own desire for changed working time arrangements," he said.
The two sides have remained in logjam since December over the dispute centred on a company call for longer working hours and the failure of Peugeot to bring pay in line with other manufacturers.
But if this last-ditch effort fails, Peugeot could find itself facing a major strike in the run-up to a British election which must be held by May 22.

The T&G received overwhelming support for strike action in the result of a ballot )which was published on Wednesday. It showed 1,720 workers in favour of striking, with 363 against. In a vote on industrial action, 1,848 were in favour, with 243 against.
The Coventry plant is Peugeot's only production facility in Britain and turned out 85,000 cars last year.
The dispute comes at a time when all car makers are facing tough sales and poor profits in Europe.

Analysts warn that Peugeot workers could be playing a dangerous game at a time when the industry is suffering from over-capacity. LMC International's director of motor research Charles Young said the Peugeot Coventry plant was known as a "low production and antiquated plant."
He added that it would not be difficult to boost capacity in Peugeot's more modern Spanish or French plants, if necessary.
